title: Mirage of the Disappearing Angel
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. The old cases/ file's culprit (Taro Hayashi) is confirmed correct by the transcript -- he already had to be manually added to the wiki-derived suspect pool since the wiki summary underplays him until the reveal, and that manual addition holds up. What the old file missed/flattened: (1) the two-condition deduction (left-handed AND able to operate a boat) that actually identifies Hayashi, built from the punch-bruise-on-right-cheek clue and the painting's revealed boat scene -- the old file only had the painting clue; (2) Ishiguro's cap is explicitly contrasted as black against the painting's white cap as a clue that clears him; (3) the Shirakawa suicide-subplot and Conan's closing coda that Aoki's kindness to Shirakawa the night before his own murder talked him out of it; (4) Mrs. Aoki, the client who opens the episode, was entirely absent from the old node list despite being present throughout. The backstory victim's name 'Nagisa Fujii' is carried over from the old file's event text since the transcript excerpt itself never states her name on-screen (she is only 'Mr. Akagi's girlfriend' in dialogue) -- flagged here rather than presented as transcript-confirmed. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Hayashi referred to the deleted camera data as a video, not photos -- a detail only the deleter or the police (who hadn't told him) could have known.
Aoki's painting right-side up shows a peaceful angel scene; turned upside down (a superior-mirage effect), the same lines resolve into a boat with a woman being thrown overboard.
The cap drawn on the culprit in the flipped painting is white, but Ishiguro's own cap -- worn every time he puts to sea -- is black.
